reason: Lens: schedule and feasibility. The kernel part can be built, and the calendar has slack. The plan as written still fails the 0.7 bar, because every honest validation step depends on a train-side input that does not exist, and the gates it sets are unlikely to pass. (1) Missing input. x138's LOWDET dump (BIOHUB_CACHE_DIR=/kaggle/working/edge_cache, LOWDET_THRESHOLD 0.3; experiments/ext_x138 cell 0 l.103-105) is written only at runtime, on the TEST clips. No lowdet dump of the 199 train videos exists: not in the repo, not in a dataset. Friend A's B35 peak cache (tools/recover_daughters.py) is a different stack: exp39 public primary, threshold 0.90, on his PC. Step 0, the SELECTION grid and the CONFIRMATION run all need 'idea 1's cache' = an x138 run on train with the edge_cache npz kept. The sibling verdict prices that at 13-16 GPU-h, with no x138 train harness and the REPAIR_DEADLINE_S 27000 guard to handle, and P(launched and done by 27 Sep 12:00) ~0.4-0.5 (v_divisions_divins-x138-lab-retune_schedule.json). Friend A has made no commits since 24 Sep 04:12 MSK. He is waiting for #34, and the x138 cache format he was asked for (raw/ckpt/dc/divnet) does not include the lowdet npz (PROMPT_FRIEND_A.md top block). (2) Agent work is about 6-9 h, not 3. tools/div_insert.py is built on two invariants the branch breaks: 'nodes are never added or removed' and 'nothing here reads files'. The work: new node records (t,z,y,x in full-res voxels plus the flags the writer and float output expect, unique ids); loading low_coords from the npz through x138's load_low_detections convention (peaks come from the detector's (1,4,4) grid, about 1.6 um quantisation); an x -> t+2 extension; and a new candidate enumerator, because candidate_triples only yields parents that already have an admissible v, so the 'extra parents' are never scored by DaughterNet today. Add byte-parity tests against the exp57b dump, a replay path on an x138 final-graph dump, and a kdn-score re-parametrisation for OOF p on x138 nodes. That kernel is hard-wired to coords_exp39.parquet (sibling verdict), which adds about 1 GPU-h and a dataset upload. (3) Gates. Step 0 kills if reach is under 8/151 or the prior is under 1:50. On the exp39 graph only 15 divisions are unreachable (151-136, b35_step_a.md), and on x138, readmit (>=0.965 within 4 um of open ends) and gapfill (>=0.5) already consume part of that pool. So '>= 8 not already covered' is a coin flip at best (GUESS P~0.4-0.5). Mirror geometry does not separate TP from FP (AUDIT3b: 7.2 vs 7.1 um, wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_divisions.notes.md l.17). That makes the grid gate (net evaluable TP >= +3 at precision >= 0.4) unlikely, GUESS P~0.3, and the in-sample detector already inflates it. (4) Probability arithmetic (GUESSES). P(#34/#35 confirm the x138 + insertion base) ~0.7 x P(train cache with lowdet on, by 27 Sep 12:00) ~0.45 x P(step 0 passes) ~0.45 x P(grid gate) ~0.3 x P(implementation and dummy clean first time) ~0.85 = ~0.04. Without the grid gate it is ~0.12. Shipped blind as a rider, P(scored) is ~0.6, but that is not the idea as described. (5) Even when scored, the probe cannot decide. The expected effect of +0.000..+0.0015 sits below the LB noise (~0.003, BRIEF), and the sibling value verdict already gives ~0 (v_metric-math_lowdet-daughter-recovery_value.json). Cited numbers check out: 121/151 direct and 136/151 window (CONTEXT l.1144, l.1198); 151/151 at +23.9% nodes, max 73% (b35_step_a.md; that reach is 'within 20 um of an eligible one-child parent', not mirror-specific); 15 unreachable and 30 TP / 2,537 FP (r1_hyp_divisions.json); LOWDET >= 0.3 with low_coords and low_score (x138 cells 0/4/5).
fix_if_any: Replace the train-cache dependency with a cheap detection-only step 0, and ship only as a capped rider. (a) Container, 25 Sep 12:00-19:00: the mirror branch in div_insert, off by default, with exact no-op parity against the exp57b DIVINS_DUMP. Mirror candidates are enumerated geometrically FIRST (lowdet x with h >= 0.9, >= 2 um from any node, |x-(2u-c1)| <= 5 um, sister 6-14.5, cos <= 0.25); only then are u and c1 scored by DaughterNet, which bounds the extra score_nodes calls. Cap 1 per video. Drop the x -> t+2 extension (fewer added nodes, less code). Also build a detection-only audit kernel (build_capture_kernel.py + x138's lowdet patch; the pre-ILP coords of exp51 == x138, per CONTEXT 25 Sep) that runs only on the ~87 train videos with GT divisions. (b) 26 Sep 00:05-~02:30, vitalii GPU after the reset: that kernel, 2 concurrent shards, about 3-5 GPU-h (2.2-3.5 min per video). (c) 26 Sep 02:30-04:30, Kaggle CPU or laptop: a GT-geometry step 0. Use the GT parent and the detected daughter for the mirror point, and GT single-child non-dividing nodes for the prior. Count only events NOT already reachable by readmit (>= 0.965 within 4 um of an open end) or gapfill (>= 0.5). Kill if fewer than 8 unique events (44b6 counted once) or a prior below 1:50 at h >= 0.9. (d) If it passes: add it as a rider on the next already-approved x138-based probe, one dummy run (~0.7 GPU-h), with the gate 'adds <= 1 node per video, runtime +< 2%, no REPAIR guard trip'. No separate LB slot, no SELECTION grid; that would need the 13-16 GPU-h x138 train run. Adopt only if LB >= base + 0.003. On a tie, keep the base (the effect is below the noise).
